draft.title: Trade links places
card: Trade is buying and selling goods and services. Goods are things you can touch, such as wheat or phones. Services are work done for others, such as banking or tourism.
Each trade links two places: the place where something is made or provided and the place where it is bought. People, money and products move between them.
Trade links places at every scale. A local shop links a farm to a town. Trade between states links cities and regions. Global trade links countries.
Exports are goods and services sold to other countries. Imports are those bought from other countries. Both link Australia to the places it trades with.
draft.remember: Every sale links the place that provides something to the place that buys it, at any scale.

a.q: Which sentence best explains how trade links two places?
opts: Goods, services and money move between them
Both places make exactly the same products
Both places are run by the same government
People from one place must move to the other
a.why: Trade links places because goods, services and money move between the seller's place and the buyer's place. The places do not need the same products, the same government or any move of people.
a.clue: Think about what moves when something is sold.

b.q: Tom grows apples near Stanthorpe in Queensland. He sells some to a local shop and ships some to a buyer in Japan. What does this show?
opts: Trade links his farm to places at different scales
Trade only links places that are far apart
Trade links places only when it crosses a border
Trade links places only through selling services
b.why: The local shop is a link at a small scale and the sale to Japan is a link at a global scale. Trade links places at every scale, not only across borders or over long distances. Apples are goods, so services are not needed.
b.clue: Compare the shop sale with the sale to Japan.

a.best: Goods, services and money move between them

b.best: Trade links his farm to places at different scales

problems.detail: All three wrong options contain 'only', and the right option is the only one without it. A student could pick the answer by spotting the absolute word, without knowing about scale.

Why (a) says trade does not need 'any move of people', but the card says 'People, money and products move between them.' The why should say people do not have to move, not that people do not move at all.
